title: Add shadow billing compare mode (dual-run meters without impacting invoices)
author: Connor O'Brien
description:
Summary: Introduces a "shadow billing compare" mode that dual-runs meter calculations (old vs new) on the same usage inputs and persists both results for diffing, without affecting invoices or the customer-facing Usage API. This is intended to support safe metering changes (token counting, retries/idempotency fixes, embeddings batching, Dedicated GPU-seconds v2) by allowing Finance/RevRec and Eng to validate deltas before any meter output is used for ledger writes.

Context / Motivation: We’ve had multiple meter changes in-flight (retry double-counting, region dimension fixes, embeddings batch accounting, Dedicated GPU-seconds v2). Historically the only way to validate meter deltas was ad-hoc queries and backfills, which makes it easy to miss edge cases (late events, partial streaming chunks, fallback routing) and increases risk of invoice disputes. This PR adds a first-class mechanism to compute both versions on live traffic and quantify expected diffs by account/model/region/day, while keeping billing ledger writes pinned to the existing “active” meter version.

Design: 1) Meter versioning: Adds a MeterVersion enum and per-meter "active" vs "shadow" selection. The active version continues to drive billing_ledger writes; the shadow version is computed in parallel and written only to billing_shadow_results.
2) Dual-run execution path: In billcalc/usage-aggregator, after we build the canonical UsageSlice (account_id, workspace_id, api_route, model, region, timestamp_bucket, dimensions), we invoke both calculators behind a shared normalization layer to ensure identical inputs (including tokenization inputs, request-id grouping, and dedupe windowing).
3) Persistence + schema: Adds a new table billing_shadow_results (Snowflake) with: run_id, meter_name, active_version, shadow_version, key dimensions, active_value, shadow_value, delta_abs, delta_pct, computed_at, and a small set of “attribution hints” (retry_count, cache_hit_rate, late_event_ratio) used for triage.
4) Metrics + alerting hooks: Emits Prometheus counters/gauges for compare coverage (percent of slices dual-run), compute lag, and delta distributions. This is intentionally not paging on delta magnitude yet; alerting is added in a follow-up once we have baseline noise levels.
5) Feature flag + safety rails: Shadow mode is gated via control-plane config: billing.shadow_compare.enabled, billing.shadow_compare.meters=[...], and billing.shadow_compare.sample_rate. When enabled, the service will: (a) compute shadow only for sampled slices; (b) never write shadow values to billing_ledger; (c) never expose shadow values via /v1/usage exports; (d) annotate runs with config hash for auditability.

Operational workflow (intended): Enable shadow compare for a target meter + shadow version (e.g., hosted_tokens:v2) at low sample_rate in staging → verify invariants → enable in prod at ~1–5% for 3–7 days → Finance/Eng review delta report (by top accounts + aggregate) → if within expected bounds, proceed with meter activation change under PM-1872 change control.

Test plan: - Unit tests: Added tests for dual-run selection logic, schema mapping, delta calculation, and “never write to ledger” invariants.
- Integration tests: Staging job executes dual-run on recorded usage fixtures including retries + streaming partials. Validates stable keys and that idempotent replays don’t multiply shadow rows.
- Load/perf: Verified added compute overhead stays under 3% CPU at sample_rate=5% on canary; most overhead is tokenization, which is already cached per UsageSlice.

Risk / Rollout: - Default OFF in all envs. - When enabled, writes to a separate table with separate retention policy (30 days) and restricted access (Finance/RevRec + Telemetry on-call). - Backfill is intentionally out of scope for this PR; we only support forward compute on incoming slices.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add dashboard panels in Console/Grafana to visualize deltas and top contributors. - Add a paging policy for sustained drift beyond threshold (once we characterize baseline noise). - Apply the same compare mode to Dedicated GPU-seconds v2 activation and embeddings batch meter fixes.

Notes for reviewers: Most of the surface area is plumbing + safety rails; the meter calculators themselves are unchanged. Please focus review on (1) ledger write invariants; (2) stable join keys between active and shadow; (3) sampling + idempotency interactions.
commits: billcalc: add MeterVersion + active/shadow configuration plumbing
usage-aggregator: dual-run execution path w/ shared normalization
tests: add invariants for "no ledger writes" + idempotent replays
docs: add runbook notes for enabling shadow compare in staging/prod
review_conversation: Nadia Rahman: Can you confirm the join key for active vs shadow rows is stable across backfills/replays? We’ve been burned by timestamp bucketing differences. Also, please ensure tokenization cache is keyed by the normalized prompt bytes, not request_id.

Connor O'Brien: Join key is (run_id, meter_name, account_id, workspace_id, bucket_start, model, region, route, dimension_hash). bucket_start comes from the canonical UsageSlice, so both calculators receive identical bucket_start. Replays: writer uses deterministic row_id = sha256(join_key) to upsert, so idempotent. Tokenization cache is keyed by normalized prompt bytes + model tokenizer version; request_id is not used.
Mei Lin: Finance will need to query this by account/day and get a "top deltas" view. Are we persisting both absolute and pct delta? Also please add an easy way to map run_id to the config used.

Connor O'Brien: Yes: delta_abs and delta_pct stored; also added config_hash + config_json to the run header table billing_shadow_runs (created in same migration). Queries can join on run_id to fetch config_json.

Cole Summers: Safety: I want a hard invariant that ledger writes cannot occur when compare mode is enabled and active_version != configured active. Right now it looks like a conditional in compute_meters. Can we add an assert/metric to detect accidental writes?

Connor O'Brien: Added an explicit guard in ledger_writer: if request_context.shadow_compare_enabled == true then we only accept active meter results (tagged is_active=true). Added a counter billing_shadow_compare_ledger_write_blocked which increments if any non-active attempt reaches the writer (should remain 0).

Logan Wright: Sampling semantics: are we sampling per request, per slice, or per account? We don’t want sampling to bias toward high-volume accounts only.
Connor O'Brien: Sampling is per UsageSlice (post-aggregation) using hash(account_id + bucket_start + meter_name) < threshold so it’s stable and evenly distributed. It will still overweight high-volume accounts in absolute row count, but coverage is stable per-account; we can also force-include accounts via billing.shadow_compare.force_accounts=[...].

Aisha Bello: Please add explicit SLO language in the runbook: compare lag and write failure behavior. Also confirm PII isn’t being written into the shadow tables.
Connor O'Brien: Updated runbook with expected lag (< 30m p95 from slice close) and failure mode (shadow failures do not block active billing). Tables include only ids/dimensions; no prompts/responses/token text is written.
release_notes: Internal: Added shadow billing compare mode to dual-run meter versions and persist diffs for validation prior to meter activation.
No customer-visible changes; billing ledger and Usage API remain driven by active meter version.
